POC & technical details: 
- Workload shape: ~60% short chat queries (avg 60 tokens), 30% embedding lookups (512-d vectors), 10% reranking across short lists. Bursty traffic (morning peaks, product launches).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for chat; p95 < 50ms for embedding retrieval (end-to-end).
- Throughput target: baseline POC showing 200 rps; target for Dedicated is 500 rps steady.
- Model preference: open/llama-family variants for cost control, Redwood-verified profiles; fallback to higher-capacity model during launches.

Cost optimization workshop takeaways (notes from session):
- Batching: recommended dynamic batching up to batch size 16 for chat tails; enables ~1.8x token throughput improvement on our sample traces. SE suggested conservative per-route max_batch=16, latency-aware batch timeout=8ms.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for common onboarding prompts + static help text cut 1.6x token spend for support-agent workload. Suggested TTLs for prefix cache = 24h for UI messages, session KV cache kept per-user for 30m.
- Quantization profiles: tested int8 (GPTQ-style) for mid-tier models gave ~2.2x perf/cost improvement with minimal BLEU/semantic-qa drop in our evals. 4-bit (QLoRA-style) recommended only for reranking/embeddings where exact generation quality less critical. Action: Redwood SE to share quant profiles and accuracy delta table.
- Unit economics model: baseline hosted API cost per 1k chat requests = ~$12 (current POC). With batching + caching + int8 quantization projected cost drop of 35-45% depending on cache hit rate. Dedicated reserved pool pricing estimate reduces per-token unit cost further but requires 6-9 month commit to achieve target ARR.
